walkthroughs.body_html:
Organisms & Biodiversity — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Organisms & Biodiversity brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Organisms & Biodiversity.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Higher Simpson's diversity index D indicates:
options: Lower biodiversity
Higher biodiversity
No biodiversity
Same biodiversity

mcqs.q: Captive breeding is an example of:
options: In situ conservation
Ex situ conservation
Reforestation
Succession

mcqs.q: Why are X-linked recessive conditions more common in males?
options: Negative feedback only operates when something goes wrong in the body.
Males have only one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele is expressed — there's no second X to mask it.
X-linked recessive conditions affect more males because the Y chromosome makes the disease worse.
X-linked conditions affect only males because females cannot inherit X-linked alleles.

mcqs.q: Why are frameshift mutations usually more severe than point substitutions?
options: X-linked conditions affect only males because females cannot inherit X-linked alleles.
Insertions/deletions of a non-multiple of 3 shift the reading frame, changing every codon downstream of the mutation.
Frameshift mutations are usually silent because cells can correct them.
Frameshifts only change the codon at the site of the mutation, like a substitution.

mcqs.q: Why is negative feedback the default mechanism in homeostasis?
options: It opposes deviations from a set point, returning the variable toward its normal value — keeping internal conditions stable.
Negative feedback amplifies changes to make them more noticeable.
Negative feedback only operates when something goes wrong in the body.
Frameshift mutations are usually silent because cells can correct them.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Biodiversity”?
options: Variety of living organisms; measured at species, genetic and ecosystem levels.
D = 1 − Σ(n/N)², a measure of biodiversity including both richness and evenness.
Ex situ conservation; breeding endangered species in captivity to maintain gene pools and reintroduce them.
Relative abundance of different species in a community; high if abundances are similar.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Species richness”?
options: Relative abundance of different species in a community; high if abundances are similar.
Ex situ conservation; breeding endangered species in captivity to maintain gene pools and reintroduce them.
Protection and management of habitats and species to maintain biodiversity for future generations.
The number of different species in a community, ignoring relative abundance.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Simpson's index”?
options: The number of different species in a community, ignoring relative abundance.
Variety of living organisms; measured at species, genetic and ecosystem levels.
D = 1 − Σ(n/N)², a measure of biodiversity including both richness and evenness.
Ex situ conservation; breeding endangered species in captivity to maintain gene pools and reintroduce them.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Species evenness”?
options: Protection and management of habitats and species to maintain biodiversity for future generations.
D = 1 − Σ(n/N)², a measure of biodiversity including both richness and evenness.
Relative abundance of different species in a community; high if abundances are similar.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Captive breeding”?
options: The number of different species in a community, ignoring relative abundance.
Ex situ conservation; breeding endangered species in captivity to maintain gene pools and reintroduce them.
D = 1 − Σ(n/N)², a measure of biodiversity including both richness and evenness.

options: Relative abundance of different species in a community; high if abundances are similar.
Protection and management of habitats and species to maintain biodiversity for future generations.
Ex situ conservation; breeding endangered species in captivity to maintain gene pools and reintroduce them.
